title: Your Shift From Hell
description: Branching safety scenario: electrical hazards, sharps, surgical fire, laser safety, an all-hazards emergency, and mass-casualty triage. Class-wide score she controls up front.

bands.title: SAFETY CHAMPIONS
bands.text: Your team prevented multiple adverse events and survived the shift.

bands.title: YOU SURVIVED
bands.text: A few incident reports are coming, but everyone made it.

bands.title: RISK MANAGEMENT WOULD LIKE A WORD
ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
bands.text: Congratulations. You are now the subject of next year's mandatory safety module.

intro.title: CLOCK IN
intro.body:
You walk into the OR department, put your bag away, and look at today's assignment.

**OR 4 – Multiple Cases**

Your charge nurse says, *“We're short staffed today, so stay alert.”*

You have no idea how important those words are about to become.
intro.notes: Students are the CST assigned to OR 4 at 07:00 on what seems like a completely normal Tuesday.

objective.title: Your Objective
objective.body:
Keep your **patients**, **yourself**, and your **surgical team** safe until the end of the shift.

You begin with **10 Patient Safety Points**.

- Make a dangerous decision: **lose points**
- Recognize / prevent a hazard: **gain points**
- Cause a sentinel-event-level disaster: ☠️
objective.notes: Then the adventure begins. Keys: A/B/C to choose, Space to continue, D to roll, R to reveal, T to start/pause a timer, M to mute timer sounds, Backspace to undo, +/− to adjust the score.

teams.title: Form Your Teams
teams.body:
Split into **4 teams**: **Team 1**, **Team 2**, **Team 3**, and **Team 4**.

Sit together. You're a team for the whole shift.

When a round says **Teams**, talk it out together before you answer.
teams.notes: Split the class into 4 roughly equal groups now. Rounds 3 and 4 are team discussions, and Round 6 gives each team its own assignment (Water, Waste, Air, Surgery).

r1.title: Something Isn't Right
r1.body:
While setting up, you notice several things:

- A power cord has a small frayed area.
- An extension cord crosses the walking path.
- The Mayo stand feels slightly too high.
- The surgeon's rolling stool is sitting behind you.

options.feedback: Good ergonomic thinking — but you missed the more immediate **electrical hazard**.

options.text: Remove the frayed electrical cord from service.
options.feedback:
Correct. A frayed cord is an immediate **electrical hazard** — remove it from service.

Several hazards can exist at the same time. Your job is to **recognize and prioritize** them.

options.text: Move the rolling stool with your hand while sterile.
options.feedback: Your glove contacts the unsterile stool. You now have to **change your glove** — and your surgeon asks why the case hasn't started yet.

r1.notes:
Source: Intro U2 obj 19-20.pptx (frayed cords / electrical safety).
Sets up the idea that several hazards can exist simultaneously — students need to recognize and prioritize.

r2.title: The Sharps Incident
r2.body:
The procedure is underway.

The surgeon finishes suturing and says: **“Here.”**

He starts handing the loaded needle holder directly back to you.

options.what_if:
You'd **roll a die**.

- **1–2:** nothing happens… this time.
- **3–6:** **NEEDLESTICK** (−3) through your glove, then an exposure question about Standard Precautions.

Luck isn't a sharps-safety plan.
options.feedback: Confidence isn't a safety device. Let's see how this goes…

options.text: Grab the suture needle with your fingers and place it into the needle counter.
options.feedback: Never handle needles with your fingers. Use an **instrument** to handle suture needles.

options.text: Direct the surgeon to place it in the neutral zone.
options.feedback: Correct, however… the surgeon **refuses to use the neutral zone** and sets it directly on your Mayo.

r2.notes:
Source: Intro U2 obj 24-28.pptx — neutral zone; handle needles with instruments, not hands.
Correct answer: C (neutral zone, +2) — but the surgeon refuses and sets it on the Mayo, so C also leads to a die roll. A (hand to hand) → die roll. Both rolls: 1–2 safe, 3–6 needlestick.
(B = −2 was added by Jeff; the original write-up didn't score the fingers option. Edit if you want it different.)

r2_roll.title: Roll the Die
r2_roll.body:
You took it hand to hand.

- **1–2:** nothing happens.
- **3–6:** …

outcomes.title: Nothing happens… this time.
outcomes.text: You got lucky. Luck isn't a sharps-safety plan — next time, use the **neutral zone**.

outcomes.title: NEEDLESTICK!
outcomes.text: The needle goes through your glove.

r2_roll.notes: Press D (or click) to roll. Keys 1–6 force a specific result if you rolled a real die.

r2_mayo.title: Roll the Die
r2_mayo.body:
You failed to secure your sharps in a timely manner.

- **1–2:** nothing happens.
- **3–6:** …

outcomes.title: Nothing happens… this time.
outcomes.text: You got lucky. A loose sharp on the Mayo is an injury waiting to happen — **secure it right away**.

outcomes.title: NEEDLESTICK!
outcomes.text: The needle goes through your glove.

r2_mayo.notes:
Reached from C: the surgeon refused the neutral zone and set the loaded needle holder on the Mayo.
Press D (or click) to roll. Keys 1–6 force a specific result if you rolled a real die.

exposure.title: Percutaneous Injury
exposure.body:
You just sustained a percutaneous injury from a **contaminated needle**.

The patient's chart doesn't identify HIV, HBV, or HCV.
exposure.prompt: Is this patient treated differently because their chart doesn't identify HIV, HBV, or HCV?

options.feedback: No — **Standard Precautions** consider *all* patients potentially infectious for bloodborne pathogens.
Correct. **Standard Precautions** consider *all* patients potentially infectious for bloodborne pathogens.

exposure.notes: Source: Intro U2 obj 24-28.pptx. Then return to the main storyline.

r3.title: “Do You Smell Something?”
r3.body:
The patient is receiving **oxygen via nasal cannula**.

The circulator has just finished an **alcohol-based prep**.

The surgeon says: **“Let's drape. I'm already running behind.”**
r3.prompt: As the CST, what do you do?

options.text: Ask whether the prep is completely dry before handing off the drapes.
options.feedback: Correct. The CST **can wait to hand the drapes or knife until the prep is dry**.

options.text: Hand off the drapes immediately. The circulator is responsible for prep.
options.what_if:
The prep is still wet. The surgeon activates the ESU.

**WHOOSH.** The drapes ignite near the patient's head: **SURGICAL FIRE** (−5 ☠️).

Prep isn't only the circulator's concern — the CST can hold the drapes until the prep is dry.
options.feedback: You hand off the drapes. The surgeon reaches for the ESU…

options.text: Drape now but keep saline nearby just in case.
options.what_if:
The prep is still wet. The surgeon activates the ESU.

**WHOOSH.** The drapes ignite near the patient's head: **SURGICAL FIRE** (−5 ☠️).

Saline nearby is a plan to put out a fire, not to prevent one.
options.feedback: A plan to put out a fire isn't a plan to prevent one. The surgeon reaches for the ESU…

r3.notes:
Source: Intro U2 obj 21-23.pptx — CST can wait to hand drapes/knife until the prep is dry.
Correct answer: A. B or C → SURGICAL FIRE (−5 ☠️). A → 'what you prevented'.

fire.title: 🔥 SURGICAL FIRE!
fire.body:
The surgeon activates the ESU.

**WHOOSH.**

The drapes ignite near the patient's head.
fire.prompt: Teams — **20 seconds**: identify the **THREE elements of the fire triangle** currently present.

reveal.title: The Fire Triangle
steps: **Bonus:** Which element did the CST have the most control over?

fire.notes:
Source: Intro U2 obj 21-23.pptx (fire triangle).
Press R once per element as the class calls them out. The 4th press shows the bonus question, which is meant to start a class discussion.

fire_prevented.title: 🧯 Fire Prevented
fire_prevented.body:
You waited until the prep was dry. The surgeon activates the ESU — and nothing happens.

Here's what *would* have happened: **WHOOSH** — the drapes ignite near the patient's head.
fire_prevented.prompt: Teams — **20 seconds**: identify the **THREE elements of the fire triangle** that were present.

reveal.title: The Fire Triangle
steps: **Bonus:** Which element did the CST have the most control over?

fire_prevented.notes:
Source: Intro U2 obj 21-23.pptx. Same fire-triangle discussion, framed as the disaster they prevented.
Press R once per element as the class calls them out.

r4.title: Laser Danger
r4.body:
You're asked to **give lunch to a tech**.

You enter their OR, where a **laser case** is set up.
r4.notes: Source: Intro U2 obj 21-23.pptx (laser safety). Next slide shows what they find in the room.

r4_room.title: Laser Danger
r4_room.body:
You immediately notice:

- No warning sign on the door
- Door propped open
- Surgeon wearing jewelry
- Staff wearing regular protective eyewear
- Laser sitting in READY mode while nobody is using it
r4_room.prompt:
In your teams, you have **60 seconds** to discuss.

You may correct only **THREE** things before the procedure begins. What do you choose — and why?

reveal.title: Trick question.
steps: You don't pick three. **The procedure shouldn't proceed until the safety issues are corrected.**
Laser on **standby** when it isn't actively being used

r4_room.notes:
Source: Intro U2 obj 21-23.pptx (laser safety). Start the 60s timer, then let each team give its three before you reveal.
The timer is deliberate production pressure. The reveal is that it doesn't count. Press R repeatedly to walk through each correction.

r5.title: And Then the Building Shakes
r5.body:
You're setting up for your next case.

Suddenly: **BOOM.**

The lights flicker. The floor moves. An overhead monitor swings. Equipment starts rolling.

The hospital announces an **emergency response**.

options.text: Continue preparing your room until someone tells you otherwise.
options.feedback: The emergency announcement *is* someone telling you otherwise. Follow the facility plan and report for your assigned role.

options.text: Leave immediately and check on family.
options.feedback: Walking out abandons your patients and your team. Follow the **facility emergency operations plan**.

options.text: Follow the facility emergency operations plan / incident command structure and await your assigned role.
options.feedback:
Correct.

**Your normal job description just became much less important.**

During emergencies, CSTs may encounter patients requiring emergency surgery or may need to perform duties in other departments.

r5.notes:
Source: Intro U2 obj 29 All-Hazards Safety.pptx.
(B = −2 was added by Jeff; the original write-up only scored C.)

r6.title: Hospital Survival
r6.body:
- The earthquake damaged the **municipal water system** — the hospital has intermittent water pressure.
- The ED is **receiving casualties**.
- Normal **biohazard waste pickup** is unavailable.
- There are reports of a **chemical release** several blocks away.
r6.notes:
Source: Intro U2 obj 29 All-Hazards Safety.pptx.
Read the update and let it land. Next slide gives each team its assignment.

r6_assign.title: Your Assignments
r6_assign.prompt: Each team has its own assignment. You have **1 minute to prepare** your briefing for Incident Command.

teams.name: Team 1: WATER
teams.prompt: How could loss of water affect surgical services and patient care?

teams.name: Team 2: WASTE
teams.prompt: What happens when normal biohazard waste disposal isn't available?

teams.name: Team 3: AIR
teams.prompt: How might the hospital protect patients/staff from contaminated outside air?

teams.name: Team 4: SURGERY
teams.prompt: Which surgical services should continue, and what should happen to elective cases?

r6_assign.notes:
Source: Intro U2 obj 29 All-Hazards Safety.pptx — maintaining care, water supply, atmospheric contamination, waste management.
“You're all in your 4 groups. You now have 1 minute to prepare your response.” Then start the timer (T).

r6_brief.title: Brief Incident Command
r6_brief.body: Time's up. Each team gets **60 seconds** to brief Incident Command.
r6_brief.prompt: You have **60 seconds** to brief Incident Command.
r6_brief.notes:
One team at a time: the active team's card is highlighted. Press T to start that team's 60 seconds (no ticking, it beeps when time is up). Space moves to the next team with a fresh timer; after Team 4, Space continues.
Listen for: maintaining care, water supply, atmospheric contamination, waste management.

mci.title: Mass Casualty
mci.body:
Multiple casualties arrive.

Supplies are limited. Staff are limited. OR availability is limited.

**You cannot treat everyone in the order they arrive.**

cards.label: Patient B
cards.text: 68-year-old, suspected ruptured abdominal aneurysm, profoundly hypotensive.

cards.label: Patient C
cards.text: 7-year-old, abdominal injury, currently stable but worsening.

cards.label: Patient D
cards.text: 35-year-old hospital employee, severe laceration with controlled bleeding.

cards.label: Patient E
cards.text: 44-year-old with devastating head injury and extremely poor likelihood of survival despite major resource utilization.

reveal.title: Before you decide…
reveal.body: **What information do you need before you can make this decision?**

mci.notes:
Don't give the “correct” answer at first — ask what information they need.
Leads into: triage, casualty response, personal/professional responsibilities, contamination control, moral/ethical issues (end of Intro U2 obj 29 All-Hazards Safety.pptx).
Print button prints the patient cards.
Drag the patient cards to rank them while the class debates; the rank numbers update as you move them.

end.title: End of Shift
end.body: Time to clock out. Let's total the points.
end.notes: Score bands: 15+ Safety Champions · 10–14 You Survived · 5–9 Risk Management · 0–4 Root Cause Analysis.
